name: SOAP
tagline: Give Stuntman the provider's WSDL and it answers like the SOAP endpoint: operations, XSD checks, faults, WS-Security and XML signatures.
stands_in_for: ICP-Brasil style e-CNPJ and e-CPF certificates
Fiscal web services such as NF-e events
point: the same address with ?wsdl (XSDs served too)
the WSDL's soap:address host on :8443, Test CA trusted

capabilities.title: Service from a WSDL
capabilities.text: A URL, a file or the text: one operation per WSDL operation, a default answer from the response type, each declared fault as a named answer.

capabilities.title: Picks the operation
capabilities.text: By SOAPAction (1.1 header or 1.2 action), or by the element in soap:Body. Unknown operations go to Unmatched with the envelope.

capabilities.title: Checks bodies against XSD
capabilities.text: Missing fields, wrong types and unknown elements get the provider's Sender fault naming the field.

capabilities.title: Faults are answers
capabilities.text: A fault has a code (Sender or Receiver), a reason template and a detail element. It goes out with HTTP 500, as real stacks send it.

capabilities.title: WS-Security
capabilities.text: UsernameToken present (any) or with matching user and password; a wrong one gets the security-token fault.

capabilities.title: XML signatures
capabilities.text: Checks each enveloped ds:Signature (RSA-SHA1 or SHA256, C14N) and signs an element of the answers with the service's own e-CNPJ.

capabilities.title: mTLS with a CNPJ
capabilities.text: On :8443 the app's certificate must be signed by the Test CA, valid and carry a CNPJ; steps read it as client_cnpj.

capabilities.title: Callbacks as SOAP
capabilities.text: send steps post an envelope with the callback's SOAPAction; send_callback calls the app's endpoint on demand.

capabilities.title: Re-import keeps your work
capabilities.text: A new WSDL adds operations with default answers; your steps, answers, data and security stay.

excerpts.title: Operations from the WSDL, with their steps

callouts.title: One per WSDL operation
callouts.text: Each with its SOAPAction and calls today; the request and response types come from the WSDL.

callouts.title: Receive
callouts.text: The envelope is checked against the WSDL's XSD and the WS-Security UsernameToken.

callouts.title: Decide
callouts.text: First match wins: a cargo value over the limit gets the coverage_exceeded fault.

callouts.title: Re-import WSDL
callouts.text: Reads a new WSDL and keeps your steps; the served WSDL is one click away.

callouts.title: Operation it lacks
callouts.text: A call for an operation the WSDL does not have gets a Sender fault and shows in Unmatched.

excerpts.title: A fault is a named answer

callouts.title: Faults from the WSDL
callouts.text: Declared faults arrive as answers, next to each operation's default response.

callouts.title: Response or Fault
callouts.text: The same answer editor; Fault adds code, reason and detail.

callouts.title: Code and status
callouts.text: Sender or Receiver (Client and Server for SOAP 1.1), sent with HTTP 500 unless you set another.

callouts.title: Detail from the XSD
callouts.text: The fault's detail element is a template, checked against the WSDL's fault type.

callouts.title: What the app gets
callouts.text: The whole envelope in the call's SOAP version, filled from the last call.

excerpts.title: mTLS, ICP certificates and XML signatures

callouts.title: Require a client certificate
callouts.text: On HTTPS a missing certificate fails the handshake; one not signed by the Test CA is refused.

callouts.title: Must carry a CNPJ
callouts.text: ICP-Brasil style: the certificate needs OID 2.16.76.1.3.3. An e-CPF or an expired one fails.

callouts.title: Check each request's signature
callouts.text: A tampered or unsigned document gets the signature_invalid answer, or a Sender fault.

callouts.title: Sign the answers
callouts.text: The named element of each answer is signed with the service's own certificate. Faults are not signed.

callouts.title: Test certificates
callouts.text: Synthetic e-CNPJ or e-CPF as .pfx and PEM; ask for an expired or untrusted one on purpose.

provoke.name: A declared fault
provoke.what: Any fault the WSDL declares, on the next calls
provoke.how: force_answer coverage_exceeded, or a decide rule

provoke.name: A fault it does not declare
provoke.what: A new fault with your code, reason and detail

provoke.name: Validation fault
provoke.what: A body that breaks the XSD gets the provider's Sender fault naming the field
provoke.how: send a bad body, or tighten types

provoke.name: VersionMismatch
provoke.what: A SOAP 1.1 envelope sent to a 1.2 service, or the reverse

provoke.name: Refused credentials
provoke.what: The security token could not be authenticated or authorized
provoke.how: security: username_token and a wrong password

provoke.name: Refused XML signature
provoke.what: A missing, broken or tampered ds:Signature

provoke.name: Refused client certificate
provoke.what: No certificate, an e-CPF, an expired or an untrusted one fails the handshake

provoke.name: Server fault
provoke.what: 500 goes out as a Receiver fault

provoke.name: Slow or dropped
provoke.what: Latency, reset, empty, timeout, 503 or an HTML page

provoke.name: Unknown operation
provoke.what: A SOAPAction the WSDL lacks gets a Sender fault and lands in Unmatched

advantages.title: No provider copy needed
advantages.text: The WSDL is enough: no recording, no running SOAP stack, no VPN to a homologation server.

advantages.title: Every fault on demand
advantages.text: Faults that a test environment almost never returns come on the next call, then stop.

advantages.title: Certificates without paperwork
advantages.text: Synthetic e-CNPJ and e-CPF test certificates in one call, valid, expired or untrusted.

advantages.title: Envelopes you can read
advantages.text: Each call shows the operation picked, the checks it passed and the raw envelopes in and out.

agent.prompt: Stand in for the insurer's SOAP service from its WSDL and check how we handle the coverage fault.
steps: RegisterShipment answered the CoverageExceeded fault, HTTP 500
tools: A SOAP service from a WSDL (URL, file or text)
Reads the WSDL again and keeps your steps
Operations, SOAPActions and the served WSDL's URL
Runs an envelope through the service; nothing is kept
Calls the app's endpoint as the provider would
With fault, makes an answer a SOAP fault
An ICP-Brasil style e-CNPJ or e-CPF test certificate
Signs an element of an XML document
Checks every ds:Signature of a document

notes: WSDL 1.1 document/literal only: no WSDL 2.0, RPC/encoded or MTOM.
WS-Security covers UsernameToken with a plain-text password, not WS-Security signatures, encryption or timestamps.
